anchor: O Brignall banks are wild and fair
note: Banks: here, wooded hillsides along a river. Brignall is a village in northern England.

anchor: And as I rode by Dalton-Hall
note: Hall: a nobleman’s large country house.

anchor: Beneath the turrets high
note: Turrets: small towers built onto the corner of a castle.

anchor: As blithe as Queen of May
note: Blithe: cheerful, light of heart. The Queen of May was a girl crowned at the spring festival.

anchor: I read you by your bugle-horn
note: Bugle-horn: a small brass horn used for hunting or giving signals.

anchor: And by your palfrey good
note: Palfrey: a gentle saddle horse, ridden by ladies.

anchor: I read you for a ranger sworn
note: Ranger: a keeper of a royal forest.

anchor: With burnish’d brand and musketoon
note: Burnish’d: polished. Brand: a sword. Musketoon: a short, wide-mouthed musket.

anchor: I read you for a bold Dragoon
note: Dragoon: a mounted soldier who carried a gun.

anchor: That lists the tuck of drum
note: Lists: listens to. The tuck of drum is the beat of the drum.

anchor: But when the beetle sounds his hum
note: Beetle: here, the beetle that flies at dusk with a humming sound.

anchor: Yet mickle must the maiden dare
note: Mickle: much, a great deal (Scots).

anchor: The fiend whose lantern lights the mead
note: Fiend: a devil. The “lantern” is the will-o’-the-wisp, a flickering light over marshes. Mead: a meadow.

anchor: Sae comely to be seen
note: Sae: so (Scots). Comely: pleasing to look at.

anchor: But aye she loot the tears doon fa’
note: Aye: always. Loot: let. Doon fa’: fall down (Scots).

anchor: Now let this wilfu’ grief be done
note: Wilfu’: willful, stubborn, set on its own way.

anchor: Nor braid to bind your hair
note: Braid: a ribbon or cord used to bind or trim the hair.

anchor: Nor mettled hound, nor managed hawk
note: Mettled: spirited, full of courage. Managed: trained.

anchor: The kirk was deck’d at morning-tide
note: Kirk: the Scots word for a church.

anchor: They sought her baith by bower and ha’
note: Baith: both. Ha’: hall. Bower: a lady’s private room.

anchor: She’s o’er the Border, and awa’
note: The Border is the line between Scotland and England. Awa’ means “away.”

anchor: by lattice high
note: Lattice: a window of crossed strips of wood or metal.

anchor: Sings high-born Cavalier
note: Cavalier: a gallant gentleman, especially a horseman or knight.

anchor: To pull the thorn thy brow to braid
note: Braid: to weave together. The thorn is a symbol of a hard lot.

anchor: And press the rue for wine
note: Rue: a bitter herb, a sign of sorrow.

anchor: A lightsome eye, a soldier’s mien
note: Lightsome: lively, light-hearted. Mien: a person’s bearing and manner.

anchor: A doublet of the Lincoln green
note: Doublet: a man’s close-fitting jacket. Lincoln green was a green cloth made in Lincoln, worn by outlaws and foresters.

anchor: The morn is merry June, I trow
note: Trow: to believe, to suppose.

anchor: The rose is budding fain
note: Fain: gladly, willingly, with pleasure.

anchor: He turn’d his charger as he spake
note: Charger: a horse trained for battle.

anchor: a sultry hectic hue
note: Hectic: here, a flushed red, as in a fever.

anchor: Ere scarce a distant form was kenn’d
note: Kenn’d: seen, known from afar. Ere: before.

anchor: And o’er the battlement did bend
note: Battlement: the notched wall around a castle’s roof.

anchor: Lost in his courser’s prancing
note: Courser: a swift, spirited horse.

anchor: Gathering Song of Donald the Black
note: Pibroch: music for the Highland bagpipe, here a war call.

anchor: Summon Clan Conuil
note: Clan: a Scottish Highland tribe whose members share a family name and a chief.

anchor: The war-pipe and pennon
note: Pennon: a long narrow flag carried on a lance.

anchor: Broadswords and targes
note: Broadswords: heavy swords with wide blades. Targes: small round shields.

anchor: Chief, vassal, page and groom
note: Vassal: a person who served a lord in return for protection. Page: a boy attendant.

anchor: Cast your plaids, draw your blades
note: Plaids: long woolen cloaks in tartan, worn by Highland men.

anchor: Knell for the onset!
note: Knell: the slow ringing of a bell. Onset: an attack.

anchor: When six braw gentlemen
note: Braw: fine, handsome, well dressed (Scots).

anchor: The gray-headed sexton
note: Sexton: a church worker who looks after the building and digs graves.

anchor: That delves the grave duly
note: Delves: digs, as one digs a grave.

anchor: The glowworm o’er grave and stone
note: Glowworm: a beetle whose larvae give off a soft light at night.

anchor: Coronach
note: Coronach: in Scotland, a song of mourning for a dead person.

anchor: Waft the leaves that are serest
note: Serest: driest and most withered.

anchor: Fleet foot on the correi
note: Correi: a hollow in a hillside where game takes shelter.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 234, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: Sage counsel in cumber
note: Cumber: trouble, distress, a heavy burden.
source: F. T. Palgrave, The Golden Treasury (1861), Palgrave’s Notes, Poem 234, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19221

anchor: Red hand in the foray
note: Foray: a raid, a quick attack for plunder.

anchor: Nor tempt the stormy firth to-day
note: Firth: a narrow arm of the sea, an estuary in Scotland.

anchor: To inch and rock the sea-mews fly
note: Inch: a small island. Sea-mews: sea gulls.

anchor: A wet shroud swathed round lady gay
note: Shroud: a cloth wrapped round a corpse. Swathed: wrapped.

anchor: Lord Lindesay’s heir To-night at Roslin leads the ball
note: Roslin is a village and castle near Edinburgh, home of the Sinclair family and their chapel.

anchor: Sheathed in his iron panoply
note: Panoply: a full suit of armor.

anchor: Deep sacristy and altar’s pale
note: Sacristy: a room in a church where sacred objects are kept.

anchor: Blazed every rose-carved buttress fair
note: Buttress: a stone support built against a wall.

anchor: The lordly line of high Saint Clair
note: Saint Clair is a form of Sinclair, an old Scottish noble family, whose lords were buried at Roslin.

anchor: The dirge of lovely Rosabelle
note: Dirge: a slow, sad song of mourning.

anchor: Hounds are in their couples yelling
note: Couples: pairs of hounds leashed together.

anchor: Diamonds on the brake are gleaming
note: Brake: a thicket of bushes and brambles.

anchor: When ’gainst the oak his antlers fray’d
note: Fray’d: rubbed. A stag scrapes his antlers against trees.

anchor: You shall see him brought to bay
note: Brought to bay: cornered by hounds, unable to run any farther.

anchor: Time, stern huntsman! who can baulk
note: Baulk: to hold back, to check or dodge.

anchor: Staunch as hound and fleet as hawk
note: Staunch: loyal and steady. Fleet: swift.

anchor: Yet Leonard tarries long
note: Tarries: waits, lingers, is late in coming.
